blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A hotel authorizes 400.00 on a card and gets approval code B20931. At checkout the bill is 352.00. The acquirer's clearing system builds the presentment from the hotel's batch file, which carries the card, the amount and the date, but no approval code. The account held 1,000.00 before the stay. Once the issuer has posted the presentment, how much can the cardholder spend?

options.text: 648.00, since the issuer posts 352.00 and releases the 400.00 hold it finds by card and amount
options.says: without the approval code the issuer can't tell which hold the record completes (19.1), so the hold stays

options.text: 248.00, since the issuer posts 352.00 and the 400.00 hold stays until it lapses
options.says: 19.1: a record without DE 38 is posted, and the hold it should release stays until it lapses

options.text: 600.00, since the issuer posts the authorized 400.00 and that posting replaces the hold
options.says: the issuer posts the presented amount, 352.00; the authorized amount is not what the record carries (19.1)

options.text: 1,000.00, since the issuer refuses a presentment without a code and posts nothing
options.says: in 19.1 the issuer posts the record without field 38; only the hold release fails

origin.section: 19.1. A Clearing Record Carries the Final Amount and the Approval It Completes

questions.stem: A network's cutover is 17:00 in its own zone. A purchase of 64.00 is approved on Tuesday at 16:58 with Tuesday's DE 15. Its answer never reaches the terminal, the acquirer reverses it, and the 0420 is acknowledged at 17:03 with Wednesday's DE 15. How do the two ends count it in their reconciliation totals?

options.text: Tuesday holds the debit and Wednesday the debit reversal, since each message counts on the day of its own DE 15
options.says: 19.2: a message that crosses the cutover counts on its own day, at both ends

options.text: Tuesday holds the debit and the debit reversal, since a reversal counts on the DE 15 day of the original it names
options.says: the reversal carries its own DE 15 and counts on that day (19.2)

options.text: Neither day holds the purchase or the reversal, since the reversal cancels the debit whatever its DE 15 says
options.says: a reversal is counted in fields of its own and the debit stays counted (19.3)

options.text: Neither day holds the debit, since the reversal with Wednesday's DE 15 takes it off Tuesday's debit count
options.says: reversals are not subtracted from the debits; the subtracting counter is answered out of balance (19.3)

origin.section: 19.2. A Transaction Belongs to the Business Day That the Network's Cutover Gives It

questions.stem: Your switch sends Thursday's totals in an 0500. The network answers with an 0510 that carries DE 39 00 and DE 66 2. What follows from that answer?

options.text: The network settles Thursday by your totals, since its 0510 accepted the request with 39=00
options.says: DE 39 00 says the request was processed; settlement still pays by the network's records (19.4)

options.text: The network settles Thursday by its own records, since the 0510 corrects nothing and moves no money
options.says: 19.4: no money moves with an 0510 and neither side's totals are corrected; the 2 starts the search for the transactions

options.text: Your switch reverses the transactions the network missed, since the 2 says some of them never arrived
options.says: 19.4: a 2 is no reason to reverse anything, since a reversal is for a request whose outcome is unknown; the transactions are found by matching (19.5)

options.text: Your switch sends the 0500 again with a new STAN, since the 2 asks for the day to be counted again
options.says: 19.4: a 2 is no reason to send the 0500 again; only an unanswered 0500 is sent again

origin.section: 19.4. The Receiver Compares Every Total, Because Equal Nets Can Hide Different Counts

questions.stem: A sale of 75.00 was made on 2 March and presented on 3 March. On 14 April the issuer charges it back as duplicate processing. In which settlement do the 75.00 move?

options.text: In the settlement of 14 April, since the chargeback is a new record that moves money again
options.says: 19.5: a chargeback debits the acquirer in the clearing and settlement of the day it arrives

options.text: In the settlement of 2 March, since the chargeback corrects the record of the sale it disputes
options.says: a dispute arrives as a new record on a later day; nothing reopens the day of the sale (19.5)

options.text: In no settlement at all, since a chargeback is settled between the merchant and the cardholder
options.says: the chargeback debits the acquirer in clearing and settlement (19.5)

options.text: In the settlement of 3 March, since the chargeback quotes the ARN of that day's presentment
options.says: the ARN finds the presentment; the money moves on the day the chargeback arrives (19.5)

origin.section: 19.5. Matching Puts Every Record in One Category, and Each Category Has an Owner

concepts: A message delivered after the cutover counts on the day of its own DE 15 at both ends, not on its original's day.
A chargeback is a new record that quotes the ARN and moves money in the clearing and settlement of the day it arrives.
A clearing record carries the final amount and the approval code that ties it to its authorization; without the code the issuer posts the sale and keeps the hold.
An 0510 moves no money and corrects no totals; a 2 starts the search for the transactions, and an unanswered 0500 is simply sent again.
